description: Reads a workbook. By default the whole current document as markdown, with its tabs. Narrow it with `tab`; a `section` (the prose under a heading, in your own words); a `table` (as data, in your own words); or `outline` for its headings, each with an `address` you can pass back to read just those. `version` reads an earlier version; `schema` returns its data-model rules; `notes` what its runs have learned about this account; `affected_by` every section an edit you describe would change. A 3D (glb) workbook also comes back with a picture of the model, from the angles in `views` (or `azimuth`/`elevation`), so you can see what an edit did.

address.description: An `address` an outline gave: just those sections.

affected_by.description: An edit, in your own words: answers with every section it would change.

azimuth.description: For a 3D workbook: one picture from this angle round the model, in degrees from the front (90 is the right side). Instead of `views`.

elevation.description: With `azimuth`: degrees above the horizon (0 level, 89 from above).

image_width.description: For a 3D workbook: the picture's width in pixels, 256 to 1024. Default 768.

notes.description: true for the notes its runs keep about this account.

outline.description: true for its headings only, each with an address.

schema.description: true for the workbook's schema: the rules every edit must hold.

section.description: Which section, in your own words.

table.description: Which table, in your own words.

views.description: For a 3D (glb) workbook: the angles to picture the model from, up to 4. Default one three-quarter view (its own camera when it has one).

wait_after.description: The version you hold: answers when the workbook moves past it (at once if it has), with the tabs that changed, so you read only those. Waits up to `seconds` (25; at most 55).

name: read_workbook
title: Read a workbook
